_comment: Behavior spec for the mdcalc language. test/evaluator.test.js asserts
every case here, and the app re-runs them all on each open (app.js
selfTest), alerting only on failure. Change language behavior by
changing this file first; the suite then fails until the evaluator
agrees. 'expected' has exactly one entry per input line; an empty
string means the line shows nothing.
THE PROSE RULE (what makes documents Markdown-compatible-ish): a line
is math if it parses as math; any line that fails the grammar is prose
and shows nothing. There is no list of Markdown constructs anywhere --
headings, bullets, tables, and sentences are silent purely because
they do not parse. 'error' appears only where intent to compute is
unambiguous: assignments, and lines that parsed but failed numerically.
The 'edge:' cases pin semantics that plain JavaScript would get wrong
by default -- floor division and modulo on negatives, '**' vs unary
minus, half-to-even rounding, and errors where JS silently produces
